transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 min | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Natasha (Sentinel Head of ML), Mark (Infra Lead), Jenna (CTO)

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex Morales from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Really quick round the table?
00:08 Natasha: Hi I'm Natasha Roman, Head of ML at Sentinel. We're looking at embedding/chat features across our analytics product.
00:14 Mark: Mark Liu, infra. I'm the person who's gonna worry about networking, VPC and costs.
00:18 Jenna: Jenna Park, CTO. High level owner here — budget and timeline.
00:22 Alex: Awesome. Priya, want to intro yourself?
00:24 Priya: Hey, Priya Shah, solutions engineer. I'll be the technical point for performance and cost stuff.
00:30 Alex: Goal for today is to go through unit economics — per token cost, what levers we have like batching and caching, and which deployment mode makes sense given your constraints. Also we'll capture next steps for a quick benchmark.
00:42 Natasha: Sounds good. To be clear, we're cost sensitive — we've got like a mid-six-figure cloud budget for this project, but need predictable per-unit costs.
00:50 Alex: Got it. Can you share rough volumes?
00:53 Natasha: Currently initial roll-out target is ~20M tokens/month, could grow to 200M in 6-12 months if feature sticks. Latency target is sub 600ms p50 for generation snippets, p95 maybe 1.2s is okay.
01:08 Priya: Nice, that helps. On Redwood hosted, our baseline per-token pricing for open model variants is X cents per 1k tokens — (note: placeholder; we'll send exact tiered sheet). For Dedicated we generally do committed vCPU/GPU pricing plus a lower per-token serving fee; Private has more fixed costs but full control.
01:28 Mark: So which path gives us best predictability? We can't have wild month-to-month swings.
01:33 Priya: Dedicated reserved capacity is our usual recommendation when predictability matters — you commit to capacity and get large discounts on unit cost. Hosted is flexible but usage spikes can increase the bill; caching and batching help reduce effective tokens billed.
01:46 Natasha: Can you explain how caching and batching actually reduce billed tokens? I thought billed tokens are just what goes to the model.
01:54 Priya: Yeah, good q. Two things: prefix or KV cache — if users ask similar queries or there's a lot of shared context, we store past key/value state for short time windows so we don't re-compute prefixes, that reduces actual compute tokens. Second, batching (continuous batching) merges similar requests on GPU to amortize fixed kernel costs and reduces per-token time-cost; it doesn't change the token count but reduces compute seconds so the effective per-token compute charge goes down on Dedicated pricing models or when you use our compute-time-billing variants.
02:24 Alex: Also worth noting we expose suggestions — e.g., prompt trimming, response length caps, and per-route batching configs. All of those reduce bill.
02:31 Jenna: Ok. Natasha, interrupts: what's our most common user query size?
02:35 Natasha: Typical prompt + context ~400 tokens and we expect 50-150 token responses, so let's assume 500 tokens per request in baseline.
02:44 Priya: With that, 20M tokens/month is roughly 40k requests/month at 500 tokens each — that math helps when we show committed vGPU sizing.
02:55 Mark: I want numbers. Like, per million tokens, what's the ballpark cost hosted vs dedicated?
03:00 Priya: Rough high-level ballpark (very approximate): hosted with our standard open-model catalog could be around $8-15 per million tokens depending on model and usage profile; Dedicated reserved could get you down to $3-6 per million when amortizing committed GPUs and batching/caching. Private on-prem varies widely — hardware + ops means upfront but $2-5 per million long term if you fully amortize. We'll send exact tiers.
03:24 Natasha: Big spread. What drives the delta?
03:27 Priya: Main drivers are (1) GPU amortization — reserved capacity lets you use GPUs efficiently, (2) batching and continuous scheduling — more throughput reduces per-token kernel overhead, (3) KV/prefix cache hit rate — if you get a 30-40% hit rate, effective tokens drop a lot, (4) model size / quantization — smaller/quantized models are cheaper per token.
03:47 Mark: About caching — where's the cache stored in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Are there data residency issues?
03:54 Priya: Hosted keeps cache in our managed infra, encrypted in transit and at rest; Dedicated keeps cache in customer-dedicated pods in the region, still managed by Redwood control plane but isolated; Private lets you host cache inside your VPC or on-prem. For sensitive data you can tie KMS to keys. We'll map this in the security doc.
04:12 Jenna: Any SLA differences that affect cost? If latency SLO misses we need fallbacks — what's the impact?
04:18 Alex: We have SLA-backed latency tiers for Dedicated; Hosted has best-effort but good regional availability. For critical SLOs we recommend Dedicated with autoscale buffer and fallback policies (smaller model fallback) to preserve availability. That affects cost because you pay for reserved buffers or accept slightly higher per-token cost for fallback traffic.
04:36 Natasha: How do you model reserved capacity discounts? Are they straight % off usage or a commit fee?
04:41 Priya: Typically it's a commit to GPUs or qps for a period (monthly/annual) — you pay a reserved fee (discounted) and then a much lower per-token or per-second compute surcharge. We can show AS-IS math in the pricing sheet. Example: 1x A100-equivalent reserved might be amortized to $Y/month and yields X% off unit compute.
05:05 Mark: For our engineering team, we need to understand burst behavior. If we commit to Dedicated but get spikes, can we burst on Hosted?
05:12 Alex: Yes — hybrid routing is supported. You can route overflow to hosted, to a model variant, or to a smaller quantized model. Bursting has different billing: overflow to hosted billed at hosted rates.
05:22 Natasha: Are there specific batching settings we should use for low-latency use cases? Our p50 target is tight.
05:27 Priya: For sub-600ms p50, we recommend small max batch sizes with dynamic scheduling, keep batch windows at 10-20ms. Also enable prefix caching aggressively for conversational flows. Batching helps throughput but increases tail latency if you increase max wait time; it's a tradeoff.
05:46 Jenna: If we start with Hosted for speed of rollout, can we migrate to Dedicated later without rewriting code?
05:51 Priya: Yes, same API and routing rules. Migration is mostly about traffic cutover and adjusting configs. We also support model pinning and rollout policies so you can do canary on Dedicated.
05:59 Natasha: For budget planning, what inputs do you need from us to give a more precise cost model?
06:04 Priya: Monthly token estimates, distribution of request sizes, latency SLOs, expected cache hit rate (or whether conversation reuse exists), and whether you need geo residency.
06:14 Natasha: We'll send token estimate and 3 canonical prompts.
06:17 Alex: Great. Quick aside — for savings we usually run an initial PoC for 2 weeks to measure batching/caching hit rates and effective per-token cost. That gives you real-world numbers.
06:28 Mark: What's the typical savings observed in a PoC?
06:31 Priya: We often see 20-50% savings from naive hosted estimates once batching and caching are dialed in and model variants considered. If you quantify that, Dedicated plus good cache hit rate can halve effective unit cost in some workloads.
06:44 Jenna: Any gotchas around token accounting? Do we get billed for tokens in cache misses only?
06:49 Priya: You get billed for tokens sent to the model; cache hits avoid re-running prefixes. But some orchestration metadata still incurs negligible overhead. We'll include examples in the cost sheet.
06:59 Alex: I'll call out 3 modeled scenarios in the doc: hosted baseline, dedicated reserved, private amortized — with example numbers for 20M and 200M tokens.
07:09 Natasha: Good. For security/compliance — SOC2 is essential, and we need audit logs for model access.
07:16 Alex: We are SOC 2 Type II and provide audit logs, RBAC, SSO/SAML. For Private we can do air-gapped integrations. We'll attach the security pack.
07:26 Mark: For VPC peering and egress costs — is that our responsibility?
07:30 Priya: VPC peering egress to Redwood-managed nodes is typical cloud egress — on Dedicated we try to colocate in region to minimize egress, Private on-prem avoids cloud egress. We'll show network topology options.
07:44 Jenna: Ok let's talk timeline — can we have pricing + benchmark plan early next week?
07:49 Alex: Yes I'll send pricing sheet by Friday (2026-03-06) and Priya will send benchmark plan by Thursday (2026-03-05).
07:55 Natasha: Perfect. A couple more detailed q's — what quantized model variants do you recommend for cost-sensitivity?
08:02 Priya: For many teams a 4-bit quantized LLaMA/GGML-style variant or an optimized 8-bit variant hits a sweet spot for cost/quality. Redwood supports mixed quant and kernel selection to keep perf high. We'll recommend specific models in the follow-up.
08:18 Mark: On Dedicated, do we get access to per-route cost breakdown? Engineers will want per-endpoint token/cost dashboards.
08:23 Alex: Redwood Console exposes per-route token and cost breakdown, per-token latency, tracing. We can onboard your monitoring team in the PoC.
08:33 Natasha: For the PoC, what success metrics should we use? Cost per thousand tokens, latency p50/p95, cache hit rate, and quality drop measured on our eval set?
08:42 Priya: Exactly. We'll propose a minimal metric set in the benchmark doc: baseline cost, effective cost after caching/batching, latency, and small set of quality passes.
08:51 Jenna: One more — procurement. If we go Dedicated, how long is the contract and can we do monthly?
08:57 Alex: We offer monthly reserved or annual with better discounts. Procurement can sign monthly if needed, but discounts scale with longer commitments. We'll include contract templates.
09:08 Natasha: Thanks. Anything else?
09:11 Mark: Just an ask to run a short sample with our dataset to understand cache hit patterns.
09:15 Priya: We'll include that in the benchmark plan — small ingestion and synthetic traffic to emulate production.
09:21 Alex: Ok let's recap next steps — I'll send pricing and contract templates (2026-03-06), Priya sends benchmark plan and sample prompts (2026-03-05), Natasha will send token estimates and sample prompts (2026-03-07). We'll schedule a 30-min PoC kickoff for wk of 2026-03-09.
09:40 Natasha: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
09:44 Jenna: Thanks all.
09:46 Alex: Appreciate your time, we'll follow up.
09:50 End of call
